newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end down despite A share leap.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end down despite A share leap.

text.p: China's B share indices ended down in dull trade on Tuesday despite an A share leap with new share listings sucking cash out of the markets and Monday's suspension of Shenzhen Development Bank weakening sentiment, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.537 points or 0.63 percent to 84.944 points while the Shenzhen B index sank 1.33 points or 0.89 percent to 146.94 on turnover of HK$51 million.
Trading in the bank was suspended by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Monday afternoon due to volatile price movements and resumed Tuesday morning.

"The B share market's recent bearishness has prevented any fresh money inflow," an analyst at China Southern Securities said. "The big B share issue by Bengang Steel has also sucked out a lot of funds," the analyst said.

Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd earlier this month completed an initial public offering of 460 million B shares, raising about one billion yuan. The company has said it will list the B shares in Shenzhen in early July.
In Shanghai, Hainan Airlines' 71 million B shares will be listed on Thursday, with many investors withdrawing capital in preparation, brokers said.

"Domestic investors who have dominated recent trading are also becoming cautious, with the forthcoming listing pulling capital away from existing shares," one Shanghai broker said. "Most investors are waiting to see how the newcomer performs before making a decision." "The market seems short of positive factors to attract fresh capital into the market, and market sentiment is not going to be boosted by some speculative institutional buying alone," another broker said.
Shanghai Industrial Sewing Machine was the biggest loser on poor prospects in the Shanghai bourse, tumbling $0.012 or 8.21 to $0.134 on volume of 39,700 shares.
Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle was the most actively traded on profit-taking, falling $0.002 or 0.37 percent to $0.536 on volume of 2.0 million shares.

In the B share market, television tube maker SEG Co maintained its sharp downward trend, falling HK$0.65 or 8.50 percent to HK$7.00 on volume of 609,803 shares. The issue lost 5.56 percent on Monday. Brokers provided no reason for the issue's decline.

The Shanghai A index closed up 22.183 points or 1.65 percent to 1,362.867 points on volume of 392.0 million shares worth 5.6 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index moved up 70.881 points or 1.74 percent to 4,153.601 points.

The Shenzhen A index jumped 13.19 points or 2.93 percent to 463.59 and turnover shrank to 10.0 billion yuan from Monday's 14.5 billion yuan as some institutions held back, viewing the bank's suspension as a sign of tightened supervision by securities regulators, brokers said.
